questions.question: Which of the following best matches the definition of a polynomial function given in the text?
options: A function p(x)=a_n x^n + a_{n-1} x^{n-1} + ... + a_1 x + a_0 where n is a non-negative integer and a_n ≠ 0
A function that can contain negative integer powers of x
Any function involving radicals of x
A function whose domain is only integers
questions.answer: A function p(x)=a_n x^n + a_{n-1} x^{n-1} + ... + a_1 x + a_0 where n is a non-negative integer and a_n ≠ 0
questions.explanation: Definition 2.1 in the excerpt defines a polynomial function as p(x)=a_n x^n + ... + a_0 with n a non-negative integer and a_n ≠ 0.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: What is the domain of a polynomial function as stated in the text?
options: The set of all real numbers
questions.answer: The set of all real numbers
questions.explanation: The text states that the domain of a polynomial function is the set of all real numbers.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: What is the degree of the polynomial f(x)=3x^3 − 9x^2 + 5x + 2 as given in Example 1?
questions.explanation: Example 1 identifies f(x)=3x^3 − 9x^2 + 5x + 2 as degree 3 because the highest exponent is 3.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: What is the leading coefficient of f(x)=3x^3 − 9x^2 + 5x + 2?
questions.explanation: In Example 1 the leading coefficient is the coefficient of the highest power x^3, which is 3.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: What is the constant term of h(x)=−5x^4 + 8x^3 + 2x^2 − 3x + 7 from Example 1?
questions.explanation: Example 1 states the constant term is the constant term a_0, here 7.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a polynomial function according to the examples in the text?
questions.explanation: Example 2 explains that terms with negative exponents (like x^{−2}, x^{−1}) mean the expression is not a polynomial.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: The sum of f(x)=2x^4 + 5x^3 + x^2 + 9x + 4 and g(x)=−3x^3 + 5x^2 − 5x − 9 from Example 1 is:
questions.explanation: The solution groups like terms to give 2x^4 + (5−3)x^3 + (1+5)x^2 + (9−5)x + (4−9) = 2x^4 + 2x^3 + 6x^2 + 4x − 5.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: Compute (2x + 3)(3x^2 − 5x + 6) as in Example 3; which expression is correct?
questions.explanation: Example 3 multiplies each term and combines like terms to obtain 6x^3 − x^2 − 3x + 18.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: What does the text state about the degree of the product of two non-zero polynomials f and g of degrees m and n?
options: The degree of f·g is m + n
The degree of f·g is m − n
The degree of f·g is the larger of m and n
The degree of f·g is always zero
questions.answer: The degree of f·g is m + n
questions.explanation: Observation in Example 3 states the degree of f·g is m + n when degrees of f and g are m and n respectively.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: According to the Remainder Theorem in the text, what is the remainder when f(x) is divided by (x − c)?
questions.answer: f(c)
questions.explanation: Theorem 2.2 states that the remainder on division by (x − c) is f(c).
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: Which statement is the Factor Theorem as given in the text?
options: If f(c)=0 then x−c is a factor of f(x)
If f(x) has integer coefficients then all zeros are integers
If f(c)≠0 then x−c is a factor of f(x)
If f has degree n then it has exactly n distinct real zeros
questions.answer: If f(c)=0 then x−c is a factor of f(x)
questions.explanation: Theorem 2.3 states that if f(c)=0 then x−c is a factor of f(x), and conversely.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: In Example 6 the quotient when x^5 + 5x^3 − 2x^2 + 7 is divided by x^2 + 2x + 1 is:
questions.explanation: Example 6 shows the quotient of that division is x^3 − 2x^2 + 8x − 16 with remainder 24x + 23.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: Which description matches the Rational Zero Test as stated in the unit?
options: If q=p/q (in lowest terms) is a rational zero then p divides a_0 and q divides a_n
Any rational number is a zero of a polynomial with integer coefficients
All zeros of integer-coefficient polynomials are integers
If a_0=0 then all rational zeros are zero
questions.answer: If q=p/q (in lowest terms) is a rational zero then p divides a_0 and q divides a_n
questions.explanation: Theorem 2.5 states that for integer-coefficient polynomials, if q=p/q in lowest terms is a zero then p divides the constant term a_0 and q divides the leading coefficient a_n.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: What does the Location Theorem guarantee if f(a) and f(b) have opposite signs?
options: There is at least one zero of f between a and b
There are no zeros between a and b
f has a rational zero between a and b
f(a) and f(b) must be equal in magnitude
questions.answer: There is at least one zero of f between a and b
questions.explanation: Theorem 2.4 states that if f(a) and f(b) have opposite signs then there is at least one zero between a and b.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: From the worked example for f(x)=x^2 + 2x − 3, what is the turning point (vertex)?
questions.explanation: Completing the square gives f(x)=−4 + (x+1)^2, so the minimum occurs at x=−1 with value −4, i.e. (−1,−4).
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: For f(x)=−x^2 − 6x − 8, what is the turning point shown in the example?
questions.explanation: Completing the square yields f(x)=1 − (x+3)^2, so the maximum occurs at (−3,1) as shown in the example.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: In the wire problem (Example 1 in Applications), what is the maximum area that a rectangle made from a 56 m wire can enclose?
questions.explanation: The solution rewrites area A=−x^2 + 28x = 196 − (x−14)^2, so the maximum value is 196 m^2 attained when x=14.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: According to the same wire example, what are the dimensions of the rectangle that give the maximum area?
questions.answer: 14 m by 14 m
questions.explanation: Setting x=14 from the maximization gives y=28−x=14, so the rectangle is 14 m by 14 m (a square).
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: Given g(x)=x^3 + 4x^2 − 3x − 18 = (x + 3)^2 (x − 2) in the text, which zero has multiplicity 2?
questions.explanation: The factor (x+3) is squared, so the zero x=−3 is of multiplicity 2 as shown in the example.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: How does the graph of an even-degree polynomial with positive leading coefficient behave for large |x| according to the observations?
options: Both ends of the graph go upward (large positive)
Left end up and right end down
questions.answer: Both ends of the graph go upward (large positive)
questions.explanation: The observations note that when degree is even and leading coefficient positive, values become large positive and the graph goes upward both far to the right and left.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: The constant function f(x)=b with b≠0 is a polynomial function of degree zero.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: The note states the constant function f(x)=b (b≠0) is a polynomial function with degree zero.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: If the remainder r(x) is zero when f(x) is divided by d(x), then d(x) divides f(x) exactly.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: The Polynomial Division Theorem notes that when the remainder r(x)=0, d(x) divides f(x) exactly (division is exact).
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: The sum of two polynomial functions is not necessarily a polynomial function.
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: The text explicitly states the sum of two polynomial functions is a polynomial function.

questions.question: A polynomial function's graph is a smooth curve with no sharp corners.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: The notes state that the graph of a polynomial is a smooth curve (has no sharp corner), distinguishing it from functions like |x|.

questions.question: Define the term 'leading coefficient' for a polynomial function as given in the unit.
questions.answer: The leading coefficient is the coefficient a_n of the term a_n x^n corresponding to the highest power of x in the polynomial.
questions.explanation: In the definition section the text states a_n is called the leading coefficient and a_n x^n the leading term.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: Give the domain of any polynomial function according to the text.

questions.question: List the four fundamental operations on polynomial functions mentioned in the unit contents.
questions.answer: Addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.

questions.question: Give a one-sentence statement of the Polynomial Division Theorem as in the text.
questions.answer: If f(x) and d(x) are polynomials with d(x)≠0 and deg d ≤ deg f, then there exist unique polynomials q(x) and r(x) such that f(x)=d(x)q(x)+r(x) with r(x)=0 or deg r < deg d.
questions.explanation: Theorem 2.1 states existence and uniqueness of q(x) and r(x) with the remainder of degree less than the divisor or zero.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: State the Remainder Theorem in one sentence.
questions.answer: If f(x) is divided by (x − c) then the remainder is f(c).
questions.explanation: Theorem 2.2 shows that evaluating f at c gives the remainder upon division by x−c because (c−c)q(c)=0 leaves the constant remainder.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: What does it mean for a zero c to have multiplicity k in the polynomial f(x)?
questions.answer: It means (x−c)^k is a factor of f(x) but (x−c)^{k+1} is not, so c is a zero of multiplicity k.
questions.explanation: Definition 2.8 defines multiplicity as the exponent k such that (x−c)^k divides f(x) but (x−c)^{k+1} does not.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: Using the Factor Theorem from the unit, explain how to test whether x−c is a factor of f(x).
questions.answer: Evaluate f(c); if f(c)=0 then x−c is a factor, otherwise it is not.
questions.explanation: Theorem 2.3 states f(c)=0 implies x−c is a factor, so computing f(c) is the test.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: Summarize the Rational Zero Test procedure in one sentence.
questions.answer: List factors p of the constant term a_0 and factors q of the leading coefficient a_n, form ±p/q in lowest terms and test which values give f(q)=0 to find rational zeros.
questions.explanation: Theorem 2.5 and the listed steps instruct to take factors of a_0 and a_n, form p/q candidates and check which satisfy f=0.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: Find the two real numbers whose difference is 16 and whose product is minimum, as solved in Example 2.
questions.answer: 8 and −8
questions.explanation: Setting y=x−16 and A=x(x−16) leads to A=(x−8)^2 − 64, so minimum occurs at x=8 giving y=−8, hence 8 and −8.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: When 3x^3 − 4x^2 + b − 5 is divided by x − 2 the remainder is 10; what is b as found in the example?
questions.explanation: By the Remainder Theorem f(2)=3(2)^3 −4(2)^2 + b −5 = b + 3 = 10, so b=7 as shown in the example.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 2: Polynomial Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).
